For decades, the playbook to success for young professionals was pretty straightforward: Go to college, land an entry-level position, gain experience and climb the corporate ladder. But in today’s sluggish labor market where artificial intelligence is reshaping many entry-level roles, that playbook is quickly being rewritten. Whether you’ve been fortunate to land your first full-time role or you’re still looking for one, success in the first year of your career requires more than just a degree nowadays. With overall hiring down 20% from pre-pandemic levels, hiring managers and experts have told me time and time again that young professionals today need to be resilient, adaptable and open to opportunities that may not initially feel like the traditional first step of their career path. From going into the office in order to strengthen workplace relationships, to building up your network and being open to contract work if needed, young workers must be receptive to stepping outside the box in order to thrive in today’s economy.  Read here to learn more about the seven new rules workplace leaders say young professionals should follow to get their career off to a strong start. — Courtney Connley-Hampton, Careers Staff Writer WORK SMARTER Practical insights and advice from Forbes staff and contributors to help you succeed in your job, accelerate your career and lead smarter. 77011.subject: Backpack's execution edge
77011.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Happy Wednesday, folks! Today we look at why Backpack and xStocks have different tokenized equity market structures on Solana, and how that shows up directly in execution cost. Markets stayed mixed, with the Solana ecosystem index up another 8.0% yesterday, though the gain traces to just two tokens, META and PUMP, rather than broad ecosystem strength.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Yesterday saw the Solana ecosystem index lead again at 8.0%, more than double the next best performing sector. Launchpad (3.2%), Bittensor Ecosystem (2.7%), AI (2.2%), and Perps (2.0%) filled out the top. Equities beat most of crypto, with the NASDAQ 100 up 3.0% and the S&P 500 up 1.9% against BTC’s 0.9%. Crypto Miners took the worst of it at -3.1%, with Ethereum Eco and Lending both at -2.0%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/96259814-fcf0-4fd9-be34-273d92b8e098/image.png?t=1785900334)
Caption: 

The weekly picture shows how quickly leadership is turning over. Crypto Miners rank second at 15.1% even after yesterday’s drop, and DEXs, which sat second on the week on Monday, have given back all of those gains and are now down -1.1% . Lending is the week’s worst performer, down -10.0%, just ahead of Ethereum Eco at -9.8%. L1s are down -2.0% on the week and SOL trades near $73, down roughly -10% on the month.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a7268227-440b-40e5-a6a4-fb47575b624d/image.png?t=1785900334)
Caption: 

The Solana index gain is narrower than it appears. META, up 46.6% on the week since its Upbit listing, and PUMP, up 22.9% and roughly a third of the index by weight, produced the entire 17.8% print between them. Seven of the eleven constituents fell, led by BP at -13.7% and BONK at -7.7%, and the median constituent is down -5.4%. Solana is up because of two tokens, not because the whole ecosystem is catching a bid.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cbd4eb46-8c23-4505-8395-7ce986b09f6c/image.png?t=1785900334)
Caption:

77008.subject: How you log in to Socios.com is changing
77008.body:
We're moving to Passkey
login and retiring phone and SMS codes. Here's what it means for
you.

*****************************************************************
UPDATES TO
LOGIN AND OUR TERMS.
*****************************************************************

Hi
Novosadov Oleh,

We're updating how
you access your Socios.com account, along with our Platform Terms
and Socios.com Wallet Terms.

Here's what's changing and
what it means for you.

Logging in
with your Passkey

After 27
August 2026, you will be able to log in with your existing wallet
Passkey: your device confirms it's you with Face ID, fingerprint,
or your usual unlock method. If you already use a Passkey,
nothing changes; keep logging in exactly as you do today. Phone
number login still works for now, but we're retiring it soon, so
your Passkey will be the only way in going
forward.

Phone number and SMS
codes are going away

We're removing phone
number sign-up and SMS verification. From 27 August 2026 onwards,
your email is how you keep your account secure and how we reach
you. Please make sure the email on your account is verified so
you never lose access to your Socios.com
account.

Your
Recovery Kit protects your
wallet

If
you ever lose access to your Passkey, your Recovery Kit is the
only way to restore access to your wallet. Keep it saved
somewhere safe. If you haven't generated one yet, you can do it
anytime in Account Management.

A change
to daily Reward Points earning

As part of this terms
update, from 10 August 2026 onwards, we're removing the minimum
Reward Points guarantee. You'll keep earning Reward Points every
day your Fan Tokens are staked, based on the Reward Points Pool
and the total Fan Tokens locked at the
time.

On 10 August 2026, as
the changes go live, you may notice a short delay in Reward
Points being credited. This only affects the switch
day.

You can
review the updated terms here
